  "text": "The answer came at once: three blows, then two.

“Don’t do that,” Elias said.

His brother looked up. “That was our signal.”

They had used it as boys, knocking through the wall between their rooms when one of them could not sleep. Their mother had never known.

The constable’s boot slipped as the hatch bucked. Elias shoved the oak bar through the iron brackets beside it. Mara caught the other end and drove it home. Something struck the wood from below, hard enough to shake dust from the rafters.

Venn’s wife struggled upright. “There’s a gate where the tunnel meets the river. He took the key.”

“Venn?” Ada asked.

The woman shook her head. “The thing that came back in his boat.”

Outside, the oar knocked again. Mara swung the lantern toward the window. The boat had caught against a piling. A man lay face down across its benches, his coat dark with water. In one outstretched hand, a brass key glinted.

“I can reach him,” the constable said.

The oak bar groaned. Elias caught his sleeve. “If the gate’s open, what good is a key?”

“To close it,” Venn’s wife said.

A low scrape traveled beneath the floor, away from the hatch and toward the river wall. Then came the sound of fingernails against the planks behind the stove.

Ada pulled the woman to her feet. Mara handed Elias the lantern and took up the iron poker.

“Get the key,” she told the constable. “We’ll keep it here.”"
